content:
We need to extract formal theory: list of rules with modality, target, condition, exception, temporal, participants, quote. Must be JSON only, no markdown.

We need to parse policy for rules. The policy includes many statements. We need to extract each rule element with modality (FORBID, REQUIRE, PERMIT). For each rule, include exact verbatim quote from policy that proves it.

We need to identify rules in the policy text. Let's scan.

Main policy sections:

- "As a telecom agent, you can help users with technical support, overdue bill payment, line suspension, and plan options." This is a PERMIT? It says you can help users with those. So PERMIT target: help users with technical support, overdue bill payment, line suspension, plan options. Condition? none. Quote: "As a telecom agent, you can help users with technical support, overdue bill payment, line suspension, and plan options."

- "You should not provide any information, knowledge, or procedures not provided by the user or available tools, or give subjective recommendations or comments." This is FORBID target: provide any information, knowledge, or procedures not provided by the user or available tools, or give subjective recommendations or comments. Quote: "You should not provide any information, knowledge, or procedures not provided by the user or available tools, or give subjective recommendations or comments."

- "You should only make one tool call at a time, and if you make a tool call, you should not respond to the user simultaneously. If you respond to the user, you should not make a tool call at the same time." This is REQUIRE? It's a rule: you should only make one tool call at a time, and if you make a tool call, you should not respond to the user simultaneously. So REQUIRE target: make only one tool call at a time; also REQUIRE: if you make a tool call, you should not respond to the user simultaneously. Could be two rules. But we can combine? Better separate.

- "You should deny user requests that are against this policy." FORBID target: deny user requests that are against this policy? Actually "You should deny user requests that are against this policy." Means you must deny requests that are against policy. So REQUIRE target: deny user requests that are against this policy. Quote.

- "You should transfer the user to a human agent if and only if the request cannot be handled within the scope of your actions. To transfer, first make a tool call to transfer_to_human_agents, and then send the message 'YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.' to the user." This is REQUIRE? It says you should transfer if and only if request cannot be handled within scope. So REQUIRE target: transfer user to human agent when request cannot be handled within scope. Also specifies steps: first make tool call transfer_to_human_agents, then send message. Could be two subrules.

- "You should try your best to resolve the issue for the user before transferring the user to a human agent." REQUIRE target: try your best to resolve issue before transferring.

- Domain Basics: not rules.

- Customer Lookup: "You can look up customer information using: Phone number, Customer ID, Full name with date of birth. For name lookup, date of birth is required for verification purposes." This is PERMIT? It says you can look up... So PERMIT target: look up customer information using phone number, customer ID, full name with date of birth. Condition: for name lookup, date of birth is required. Could be condition.

- Overdue Bill Payment: many steps. Let's extract rules.

"You can help the user make a payment for an overdue bill." PERMIT target: help user make payment for overdue bill.

"To do so you need to follow these steps:" then list steps. Each step could be REQUIRE.

- "Check the bill status to make sure it is overdue." REQUIRE target: check bill status to ensure it's overdue before proceeding. Quote.

- "Check the bill amount due" REQUIRE target: check bill amount due.

- "Send the user a payment request for the overdue bill. - This will change the status of the bill to AWAITING PAYMENT." REQUIRE target: send payment request for overdue bill (which changes status to AWAITING PAYMENT). Quote.

- "Inform the user that a payment request has been sent. They should: - Check their payment requests using the check_payment_request tool." REQUIRE target: inform user that payment request sent and instruct them to check payment requests using check_payment_request tool.

- "If the user accepts the payment request, use the make_payment tool to make the payment." REQUIRE target: if user accepts payment request, use make_payment tool.

- "After the payment is made, the bill status will be updated to PAID." This is statement of fact, not rule.

- "Always check that the bill status is updated to PAID before informing the user that the bill has been paid." REQUIRE target: check bill status updated to PAID before informing user bill paid.

- "Important: - A user can only have one bill in the AWAITING PAYMENT status at a time." This is a constraint; maybe FORBID target: have more than one bill in AWAITING PAYMENT status. So FORBID target: have more than one bill in AWAITING PAYMENT status. Quote.

- "- The send payement request tool will not check if the bill is overdue. You should always check that the bill is overdue before sending a payment request." FORBID? Actually it's REQUIRE: you should always check that the bill is overdue before sending a payment request. So REQUIRE target: check bill overdue before sending payment request. Quote.

Line Suspension:

"When a line is suspended, the user will not have service." statement.

"A line can be suspended for the following reasons: - The user has an overdue bill. - The line's contract end date is in the past." statement.

"You are allowed to lift the suspension after the user has paid all their overdue bills." PERMIT target: lift suspension after user paid all overdue bills. Quote.

"You are not allowed to lift the suspension if the line's contract end date is in the past, even if the user has paid all their overdue bills." FORBID target: lift suspension if line's contract end date is in the past (even if overdue bills paid). Quote.

"After you resume the line, the user will have to reboot their device to get service." statement (maybe REQUIRE? Actually after resume, user must reboot. Could be REQUIRE: after resuming line, user must reboot device. But it's a statement of what will happen, not a rule for agent. Might not need.

Data Refueling:

"Each plan specify the maxium data usage per month. If the user's data usage for a line exceeds the plan's data limit, data connectivity will be lost." statement.

"You can add more data to the line by 'refueling' data at a price per GB specified by the plan." PERMIT target: add more data (refuel) at price per GB.

"The maximum amount of data that can be refueled is 2GB." constraint: FORBID target: refuel more than 2GB? Or PERMIT up to 2GB. We'll treat as PERMIT target: refuel up to 2GB. Quote.

"To refuel data you should: - Ask them how much data they want to refuel - Confirm the price - Apply the refueled data to the line associated with the phone number the user provided." REQUIRE steps.

Change Plan:

"You can help the user change to a different plan." PERMIT target: help user change plan.

"To do so you need to follow these steps - Make sure you know what line the user wants to change the plan for. - Gather available plans - Ask the user to select one. - Calculate the price of the new plan. - Confirm the price. - Apply the plan to the line associated with the phone number the user provided." REQUIRE steps.

Data Roaming:

"If a line is roaming enabled, the user can use their phone's data connection in areas outside their home network." statement.

"We offer data roaming to users who are traveling outside their home network." statement.

"If a user is traveling outside their home network, you should check if the line is roaming enabled. If it is not, you should enable it at no cost for the user." REQUIRE target: check line roaming enabled; if not, enable it at no cost. Quote.

Technical Support:

"You must first identify the customer." REQUIRE target: identify customer first. Quote.

Tech support policy includes many "must" statements but those are guidelines for troubleshooting; we may need to extract rules like "If check_status_bar shows airplane mode ON, guide user to toggle_airplane_mode OFF." That's a REQUIRE? Actually it's a guideline: you should guide user. Could be PERMIT? But we need to extract rules from policy. The policy includes many "If ... guide the user to use ..." which are instructions. Those are REQUIRE? The policy says "guide the user to use ..." as a procedure. So we can treat as REQUIRE target: guide user to use specific tool when condition met.

We need to extract each such rule with quote.

Given the large number, we need to be selective but still capture key rules. However the instruction: "
